lotus root-fibre (bisa); lotus stalk (mṛṇāla); lotus is Nelumbo nucifera, standard

hindi: उनमें पहली मांसधरा नाम की है, जिसमें मांस में सिरा यानी सम्भवतः शिरा, स्नायु, धमनी यानी सम्भवतः रक्तवाहिनी और स्रोतस् यानी मार्ग के फैले हुए जाल वैसे ही होते हैं जैसे भूमि पर कीचड़ वाले पानी में बिस और मृणाल यानी कमलनाल के फैले हुए जाल।
english: Of these, the first is named Māṃsadharā, in which, in the flesh, there are the spreading networks of the sirā (probably veins), snāyu (ligaments), dhamanī (probably arteries) and srotas (channels), as there are those of lotus-fibres (bisa) and lotus-stalks (mṛṇāla) in muddy water on the ground.

text_flags.why: possible: anusvāra misplaced (-ṃnāṃ for -nāṃ)
possible: plural verb bhavanti needs a plural subject; visarga lost
possible: long ā in -srotāsāṃ is a misprint of srotasām

notes: Sirā = vein/vessel (probable), dhamanī = artery (probable); sirā and dhamanī were not sharply distinguished in all texts, so these equivalents are provisional. srotas is the doctrinal term for a channel and is kept. "bhūmābiva" is read bhūmāv iva (v/b interchange in this print), "on the ground". "paṅkodake" = in muddy water. The comparison is of the spreading of lotus fibres and stalks. Words run together: prathamāmāṃsadharā = prathamā māṃsadharā.
lines_deva: तासां प्रथमामांसधरा नाम यस्यां मांसे सिरास्नायुधमनीस्रोतासां भूमाबिव पंकोदके बिसमृणालांनां प्रताना भवंति
lines_iast: tāsāṃ prathamāmāṃsadharā nāma yasyāṃ māṃse sirāsnāyudhamanīsrotāsāṃ bhūmābiva paṃkodake bisamṛṇālāṃnāṃ pratānā bhavaṃti

hindi: दूसरी रक्तधरा नाम की है; वह मांस के भीतर है। उसमें शोणित यानी रक्त रहता है, और विशेष रूप से सिराओं यानी सम्भवतः शिराओं, प्लीहा यानी तिल्ली और यकृत यानी जिगर में। और कटे हुए मांस से क्षतज यानी रक्त वैसे बहता है जैसे दूध वाले वृक्ष से दूध बहता है।
english: The second is named Raktadharā ("blood-bearing"); it lies inside the flesh. In it is blood (śoṇita), and especially in the sirā (probably veins), spleen (plīhan) and liver (yakṛt). And from the cut flesh the blood (kṣataja, "wound-born") flows, as milk flows from a milk-bearing tree.

text_flags.why: possible: śa for sa; the sense is "from the flesh" (māṃsāt ca)

notes: Run-together tokens: māṃsasyābhyaṃtaratastasyāṃ, bhavatimāṃśācca. "it lies inside the flesh" supplies the copula for the first clause (understood). kṣīriṇaḥ vṛkṣāt: a tree with milky sap (latex); kept as "milk-bearing tree".
lines_deva: द्वितीया रक्तधरा नाम मांसस्याभ्यंतरतस्तस्यां शोणितं विशेषतश्च सिराप्लीहयकृत्सु भवतिमांशाच्च क्षतात्क्षतजं वृक्षादिव क्षीरिणः क्षीरं प्रवर्त्तते
lines_iast: dvitīyā raktadharā nāma māṃsasyābhyaṃtaratastasyāṃ śoṇitaṃ viśeṣataśca sirāplīhayakṛtsu bhavatimāṃśācca kṣatātkṣatajaṃ vṛkṣādiva kṣīriṇaḥ kṣīraṃ pravarttate

words.gloss: mastu (unclear: perhaps the first member of mastuluṅga)

hindi: तीसरी मेदोधरा नाम की है। मेद यानी चर्बी उसमें, उदर में और छोटी अस्थियों में रक्त के साथ रहता है। और वही सिर में, कपाल से ढका हुआ, मस्तिष्क नाम वाला है, और अनुमानित पाठ पर मस्तुलुंग नाम वाला भी; पर बड़ी अस्थियों में मज्जा यानी अस्थि-मज्जा है।
english: The third is named Medodharā ("fat-bearing"). Fat (medas) is in it, in the belly and in the small bones, together with blood. And that same (fat), in the head, covered by the skull (kapāla), is called mastiṣka (brain), and, on a conjectural reading, mastuluṅga; but in the large bones (it is) majjā (marrow).

text_flags.why: possible: long ā of -ākhya lost (ā + ākhya -> a + khya)
possible: extra "r" (luṃgār-); luṅgākhya expected
possible: "mastu luṅgākhyaṃ" read together as the known word mastuluṅga (brain-substance); the space in the print is doubtful

notes: Run-together: caśirasi = ca śirasi. Elliptical: the verb (is called / is) of the last clause is not supplied; "(it is)" in the English only marks the carried-over construction, "that same" = medas. The joining mastu + luṅga is conjectural: mastuluṅga is a known synonym for the brain (standard) but the print separates the words and also shows an unexplained r; so the translation says "on a conjectural reading". majjā = marrow in this anatomical context (not "kernel"). udare = in the belly. mastu is also an ordinary word (whey); its reading as the first member of mastuluṅga is conjectural, as is ignoring the printed space; gram left as unclear.
lines_deva: तृतीया मेदोधरा नाम मेदो हि तस्यामुदरेऽण्वस्थिषु च सरक्तं भवति तदेव चशिरसि कपालप्रतिच्छन्नं मस्तिष्कख्यं मस्तु लुंगारख्यं च स्थूलास्थिषु तु मज्जा
lines_iast: tṛtīyā medodharā nāma medo hi tasyāmudare'ṇvasthiṣu ca saraktaṃ bhavati tadeva caśirasi kapālapraticchannaṃ mastiṣkakhyaṃ mastu luṃgārakhyaṃ ca sthūlāsthiṣu tu majjā

hindi: चौथी श्लेष्मधरा नाम की है। उसमें स्थित श्लेष्मा से जुड़ी हुई सब सन्धियाँ यानी जोड़ दृढ़ हो जाती हैं, और, अनुमानित पाठ पर, उपांग अवयवों सहित।
english: The fourth is named Śleṣmadharā ("Kapha-bearing"). Joined by the śleṣman (Kapha) situated in it, all the joints become firm, and, on a conjectural reading, together with their subsidiary parts.

text_flags.why: possible: "tas-" for "tat-" (dittography); tat-stha, "situated in it"
possible: the printed word has no sense (vākṣa); a likely intended word is sopāṅgāvayavāḥ, "with subsidiary limbs and parts"

notes: The last printed word sopāṃgāvākṣāḥ is unintelligible; it is kept unsplit with gloss "unclear" and the translation is hedged "on a conjectural reading" (sopāṅgāvayavāḥ). The doubled avagraha in śleṣmaṇā''śleṣitāḥ is a print habit (ā + ā). āśleṣita is taken as "joined, clasped" (not āśliṣṭa).
lines_deva: चतुर्थी श्लेष्मधरा नाम तस्तस्थेन हि श्लेष्मणाऽऽश्लेषिताः सर्वसंधयो दृढा भवंति सोपांगावाक्षाः
lines_iast: caturthī śleṣmadharā nāma tastasthena hi śleṣmaṇā''śleṣitāḥ sarvasaṃdhayo dṛḍhā bhavaṃti sopāṃgāvākṣāḥ

words.gloss: intestine; raw; ripe (digested); seat; resting on

hindi: पाँचवीं पुरीषधरा नाम की है। वह अन्त्र और आम यानी कच्चे तथा पक्व यानी पके के आशय पर टिकी हुई, कोष्ठ के भीतर उण्डुक यानी सम्भवतः अन्धान्त्र में स्थित मल को अलग करती है।
english: The fifth is named Purīṣadharā ("faeces-bearing"). Resting on the intestine (antra) and on the seats of the raw and the digested (āma and pakva), it separates the waste (mala) lying within the koṣṭha (storehouse), in the unduka (probably the caecum).

text_flags.why: possible: ma for sa; the feminine pronoun "sā" refers to the layer

notes: Run-together: purīṣadharānāma, hyaṃtrāmapakvāśayāśritā. The compound antrāmapakvāśayāśritā is read as "resting on the intestine and on the āma-and-pakva seats" (probably āmāśaya and pakvāśaya, cf. line 56, 68 (card 53/62)); this reading is not certain. unduka (caecum, probable; the word is also read as a large-intestine part); "within the koṣṭha, in the unduka" is one possible reading of koṣṭhāntar-unduka-stham. malam = waste or faeces; "divides" has no stated object beyond the waste.
lines_deva: पंचमी पुरीषधरानाम मा ह्यंत्रामपक्वाशयाश्रिता कोष्ठांतरुंदुकस्थं मलं विभजति
lines_iast: paṃcamī purīṣadharānāma mā hyaṃtrāmapakvāśayāśritā koṣṭhāṃtaruṃdukasthaṃ malaṃ vibhajati

words.gloss: pakva (seat of the digested); āmāśaya (seat of the raw); middle; situated
inner; fire; being the seat of
from the āmāśaya (seat of the raw)
pakvāśaya (seat of the digested); facing toward

hindi: छठी पित्तधरा नाम की है, जो पक्व यानी पके और आम यानी कच्चे के आशयों के बीच में स्थित है। वह भीतरी अग्नि का अधिष्ठान होने से आमाशय यानी सम्भवतः जठर से पक्वाशय यानी सम्भवतः बड़ी आँत की ओर उन्मुख अन्न को बल से रोककर, पित्त के तेज से सुखाती हुई पकाती है और पके हुए को छोड़ देती है।
english: The sixth is named Pittadharā ("Pitta-bearing"), situated in the middle between the seats of the digested and the raw (pakva and āmāśaya). Being the seat of the inner fire (antaragni), it holds by force the food that faces from the āmāśaya (probably the stomach) toward the pakvāśaya (probably the large intestine), and, drying it by the heat of Pitta, cooks it, and releases what is cooked.
notes: Run-together tokens: pakvāmāśayamadhyasthā, hyantaragnyadhiṣṭhānatayā''māśayāt..., śoṣayaṃtīpacati. The doubled avagraha after -ā is a print habit. pakvāmāśaya is read as pakva-(āśaya) and āmāśaya, as in line 68 (card 62). antaragni = inner (digestive) fire; adhiṣṭhānatayā = by being the seat. vidhārya = having held (retained); the object is the food, which is directed from the āmāśaya toward the pakvāśaya. Pitta is the doṣa; the layer is the one called Pittadharā.
lines_deva: षष्ठी पित्तधरा नाम पक्वामाशयमध्यस्था सा ह्यन्तरग्न्यधिष्ठानतयाऽऽमाशयात्पक्वाशयोन्मुखमन्नं बलेन विधार्य्य पित्ततेजसा शोषयंतीपचति पक्कं च विमुंचति
lines_iast: ṣaṣṭhī pittadharā nāma pakvāmāśayamadhyasthā sā hyantaragnyadhiṣṭhānatayā''māśayātpakvāśayonmukhamannaṃ balena vidhāryya pittatejasā śoṣayaṃtīpacati pakkaṃ ca vimuṃcati

words.gloss: grahaṇī (seat of digestion; duodenum or small-intestine region, disputed); name

words.gram: bahuvrīhi, f. nom. sg. (upabṛṃhitā read as a separate word)

hindi: पर दोषों से अधिष्ठित होने पर दुर्बलता के कारण केवल आम यानी कच्चा। इसलिए अन्न को ग्रहण करने से उसका फिर ग्रहणी नाम है। और उसका बल पित्त ही है, जिसका नाम अग्नि है। इसलिए वह अग्नि से सहारा पाई हुई, पुष्ट की हुई, एक ही योगक्षेम वाली होकर शरीर को चलाती है।
english: But when occupied by the doṣas, through weakness, only āma (the raw, undigested). Hence, from its taking up of food, it again has the name grahaṇī. And its strength is Pitta itself, which has the name agni (fire). Therefore, supported by the fire, strengthened, having a single welfare (yogakṣema), it keeps the body going.

text_flags.why: possible: "nāe" is not a sandhi; agninā + upastabdha gives agninopastabdha (or agninā upastabdha); the e is a misprint of o/u

notes: Elliptical first clause: no verb is supplied (daurbalyād āmam eva: "through weakness, only āma"; the sense is probably that the weakened organ yields/holds only raw, undigested matter). "asau" (that one) points back to the organ just described (the layer of line 56 (card 53)), which the text does not name here. punar is taken literally as "again"; it could also be "further/but". ekayogakṣema is parsed as a bahuvrīhi, "having a single welfare (acquisition-and-protection)", presumably shared with the fire; the parse is not certain. grahaṇī is kept as the Sanskrit term, with its modern equivalent (duodenum/small-intestine region) tagged disputed. The "doṣa" here is the humour/fault in general. Run-together tokens split by sense.
lines_deva: दोषाधिष्ठिता तु दौर्बल्यादाममेव ततोऽसावन्नस्य ग्रहणात्पुनर्ग्रहणीसंज्ञा बलं च तस्याः पित्तमेवाग्न्याभिधानमतः साऽग्निनाेपस्तब्धोपबृंहितैकयोगक्षेमा शरीरं वर्त्तयति
lines_iast: doṣādhiṣṭhitā tu daurbalyādāmameva tato'sāvannasya grahaṇātpunargrahaṇīsaṃjñā balaṃ ca tasyāḥ pittamevāgnyābhidhānamataḥ sā'gnināepastabdhopabṛṃhitaikayogakṣemā śarīraṃ varttayati

hindi: सातवीं शुक्रधरा नाम की है। वह दाहिने पार्श्व में दो अंगुल पर और बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय के द्वार के नीचे, मूत्रमार्ग पर टिकी हुई, सारे शरीर में फैलने वाली है और शुक्र यानी वीर्य को प्रवृत्त करती है।
english: The seventh is named Śukradharā ("semen-bearing"). At two aṅgulas (finger-breadths), on the right side, and below the opening of the bladder (basti), resting on the urinary passage and pervading the whole body, it sets śukra (semen) in motion.
notes: The position is rendered as printed: "at two aṅgulas on the right side and below the opening of the basti"; the exact relation (two aṅgulas from what) is not stated. basti = bladder here (urinary bladder, probable). Run-together: bastidvārasya cādho. dvyaṃgule is dvi-aṅgule.
lines_deva: सप्तमी शुक्रधरा नाम द्व्यंगुले दक्षिणे पार्श्वे बस्तिद्वारस्य चाधो मूत्रमार्गमाश्रिता सकलशरीरव्यापिनी शुक्रं प्रवर्त्तयति
lines_iast: saptamī śukradharā nāma dvyaṃgule dakṣiṇe pārśve bastidvārasya cādho mūtramārgamāśritā sakalaśarīravyāpinī śukraṃ pravarttayati

hindi: दोष, धातु और मल पहले कहे जा चुके हैं।
english: The doṣas, dhātus and malas have been stated before.
notes: Doctrinal terms kept (doṣa, dhātu, mala); no modern equivalent forced. Run-together: dhātavomalāśca. Copula understood and supplied ("have been").

words.gram: bahuvrīhi + abstract suffix, f. inst. sg.

hindi: ज्ञान की पाँच इन्द्रियाँ हैं: श्रोत्र, स्पर्शन, दर्शन, रसन और घ्राण। उनके समान भाग होने से क्रम से विषय शब्द, स्पर्श, रूप, रस और गन्ध हैं।
english: The five sense-organs of cognition (buddhīndriya) are: hearing (śrotra), touch (sparśana), sight (darśana), taste (rasana) and smell (ghrāṇa). Of these, by way of equal shares, the objects in order are sound, touch, form, taste and smell.
notes: [02.05.60] The list names the faculties; the seats (organs) are given in line 62 (card 58). Copula understood and supplied. [02.05.61] samabhāgatayā (by being of equal share) is rendered literally; it presumably means one object for each organ, in order, but the text does not say more. Copula understood and supplied.
lines_deva: पंच बुद्धींद्रियाणि श्रोत्रं स्पर्शनं दर्शनं रसनं घ्राणं च
lines_iast: paṃca buddhīṃdriyāṇi śrotraṃ sparśanaṃ darśanaṃ rasanaṃ ghrāṇaṃ ca

words.gloss: speech; anus (apāyu); genital organ (upastha); hand; foot; named

hindi: ज्ञान की पाँच इन्द्रियों के अधिष्ठान हैं: दोनों कान, त्वचा, दोनों आँखें, जीभ और दोनों नासिकाएँ। कर्म की पाँच इन्द्रियाँ हैं, जिनके नाम वाक् यानी वाणी, अपायु यानी गुदा, उपस्थ यानी जननेन्द्रिय, पाणि यानी हाथ और पाद यानी पैर हैं।
english: The five seats of the sense-organs of cognition are: the two ears, the skin, the two eyes, the tongue and the two nostrils. The five organs of action (karmendriya) are those named speech (vāk), anus (apāyu), genital organ (upastha), hand and foot.

text_flags.why: possible: "vāva-" for "vāga-" (ga -> va misprint); vāk = speech is the first of the standard five

notes: [02.05.62] Printed jivhā is the variant spelling of jihvā (normalised in `w`; recorded once). Run-together: tvagakṣiṇī, nāsikeca. Copula understood and supplied. nāsike is a dual (two nostrils / nose). [02.05.63] Copula understood and supplied. apāyu = anus, upastha = genital organ (both standard). Hindi: अपायु यानी गुदा.
lines_deva: पंच बुद्धींद्रियाधिष्ठानानि कर्णौ त्वगक्षिणी जिव्हा नासिकेच
lines_iast: paṃca buddhīṃdriyādhiṣṭhānāni karṇau tvagakṣiṇī jivhā nāsikeca

words.gloss: speaking; discharge; delight; taking; going; for the purpose

hindi: और वे भी वचन, उत्सर्ग, हर्ष, ग्रहण और गमन के लिए हैं। पर मन इन्द्रियों से परे है, क्योंकि उसका सब विषयों से अन्वय है।
english: And these too are for the purposes of speaking, discharge, delight, taking and going. But the mind (manas) is beyond the sense-organs, because of its association with all objects.
notes: [02.05.64] Run-together: tānyapica. Copula understood and supplied. The five purposes are in the same order as the five organs of line 63 (card 58) (speech, anus, genital, hand, foot); the text does not state the pairing. harṣa = delight, pleasure. [02.05.65] anvaya = association, connection (following along with); the plainest sense is kept. Copula understood and supplied.

hindi: और उसके योग से इन्द्रियों की विषयों में प्रवृत्ति होती है।
english: And it is through union with it (the mind) that the sense-organs engage with their objects.
notes: Run-together: ceṃdriyāṇām = ca indriyāṇām. tad = the mind (manas) of line 65 (card 59). Copula understood and supplied.

words.gloss: cognition; action; sense-organ; both; nature; being

hindi: और बुद्धि और कर्म दोनों इन्द्रियों के स्वभाव वाला होने से।
english: And because of having the nature of both the sense-organs of cognition and the organs of action.
notes: Elliptical: the subject (the mind, manas, from line 65 (card 59)) and the verb are carried over and are not supplied.

words.gloss: blood; Kapha; āma (raw); Pitta; pakva (digested); Vāyu; urine; receptacles

hindi: सात आशय, अनुमानित पाठ पर, क्रम से रक्त, कफ, आम यानी कच्चे, पित्त, पक्व यानी पके, वायु और मूत्र के आधार हैं।
english: The seven seats (āśaya), on a conjectural reading, are in order the receptacles of blood, Kapha, āma (the raw), Pitta, pakva (the digested), Vāyu and urine.

text_flags.why: possible: samāśayāḥ gives no sense; seven items are listed and line 69 (card 63) calls the garbhāśaya "the eighth" (aṣṭamaḥ)

notes: The seven are, in order: the seat of blood (asṛj), Kapha, āma, Pitta, pakva, Vāyu and urine. The text does not name them as āśayas beyond this list (cf. line 56 (card 53) for the pakva/āma seats). Copula understood and supplied. Hindi writes पक्व and आम as printed terms.

words.gloss: Pitta; pakva (digested); of the two seats

hindi: स्त्रियों में पित्त के आशय और पक्वाशय के बीच में आठवाँ आशय गर्भाशय यानी गर्भ का आशय है।
english: In women, between the Pitta seat and the pakva seat (pakvāśaya), the eighth seat is the garbhāśaya (womb, uterus).
notes: pittapakvāśayayoḥ is read as the dual "of the Pitta (seat) and the pakva seat (pakvāśaya)". Copula understood and supplied.

words.gloss: heart; liver; spleen; lung; unduka (caecum; probable); kidney; intestine; and so on

hindi: उनमें बँधे हुए कोष्ठ के अंग हैं: हृदय, यकृत यानी जिगर, प्लीहा यानी तिल्ली, फुप्फुस यानी फेफड़ा, उण्डुक यानी सम्भवतः अन्धान्त्र, वृक्क यानी गुर्दा, अन्त्र आदि।
english: Attached to these (seats) are the members of the koṣṭha (trunk): the heart (hṛdaya), liver (yakṛt), spleen (plīhan), lung (phupphusa), unduka (probably the caecum), kidney (vṛkka), intestine (antra) and so on.

text_flags.why: possible: "vakka" for vṛkka (kidney), the form used in line 74 (card 68) (vṛkkau)

notes: koṣṭhāṅga: members of the koṣṭha (the trunk or storehouse); kept. phupphusa = lung (standard); vṛkka = kidney (standard); unduka = probably the caecum (tag: probable; the identity is debated). Copula understood and supplied.

words.gloss: by samāna (the Vāyu so named; probable)

words.gram: n. gen. sg. pass. part. ā-√dhmā

hindi: वहाँ समान नामक वायु से फुलाए जाते हुए और देह की ऊष्मा से पकाए जाते हुए शोणित के अस्पष्ट शब्द अच्छतः से, अनुमानित पाठ पर उसके स्वच्छ भाग से, यकृत और प्लीहा उत्पन्न होते हैं।
english: There, from blood (śoṇita) being inflated by samāna (the Vāyu so named) and cooked by the body's heat, from its unclear word acchataḥ (on a conjectural reading, "from its clear part"), the liver (yakṛt) and spleen (plīhan) arise.

text_flags.why: possible: acchataḥ is not an attested form; read as accha-tas "from the clear part" by parallel with prasādāt in lines 74-75 (card 68/69); unsure

notes: The word acchato is unclear; the reading "from the clear part" is conjectural. samāna = the Vāyu so named (probable). ādhmāyamānasya is the present passive participle of ā-√dhmā (being blown up, inflated). The liver and spleen are treated together as one subject with a singular verb (jāyate). Run-together: śoṇitasyācchato.
lines_deva: तत्र समानेनाध्मायमानस्य देहोष्मणा पच्यमानस्य शोणितस्याच्छतो जायते यकृत्प्लीहा च
lines_iast: tatra samānenādhmāyamānasya dehoṣmaṇā pacyamānasya śoṇitasyācchato jāyate yakṛtplīhā ca

hindi: रक्त के झाग से फुप्फुस यानी फेफड़ा।
english: From the froth of blood, the lung (phupphusa).
notes: Elliptical: the verb jāyate (arises) is carried from line 71 (card 65) and is not supplied. GROUPING: lines 71-75 (card 65/69) appear to be one continuing statement of the origin of the organs.

hindi: रक्त के किट्ट यानी तलछट से उण्डुक यानी सम्भवतः अन्धान्त्र।
english: From the dregs (kiṭṭa) of blood, the unduka (probably the caecum).
notes: Elliptical: the verb is carried from line 71 (card 65) and is not supplied. Run-together: raktakiṭṭāduṃdukaḥ is rakta-kiṭṭāt + unduka-ḥ (the t becomes d before a vowel). unduka = probably the caecum (probable).

words.gloss: blood; fat (medas); from the clear essence

hindi: रक्त और मेद के प्रसाद यानी स्वच्छ सार से दोनों वृक्क यानी गुर्दे।
english: From the clear essence (prasāda) of blood and fat (medas), the two kidneys (vṛkka).
notes: Elliptical: the verb is carried from line 71 (card 65) and is not supplied. prasāda = the clear, refined essence; rendered the same in lines 75, 79, 82, 83 (card 69/73/75/76).

words.gloss: blood; flesh; from the clear essence

hindi: रक्त और मांस के प्रसाद यानी स्वच्छ सार से अन्त्र।
english: From the clear essence (prasāda) of blood and flesh, the intestines (antra).
notes: Elliptical: the verb is carried from line 71 (card 65) and is not supplied.

words.gloss: with a half; three; vyāma (fathom, arm-span)

hindi: वे पुरुषों में साढ़े तीन व्याम यानी फैलाई हुई दोनों बाँहों की लम्बाई के होते हैं।
english: Those (intestines) are three and a half vyāmas (fathoms, arm-spans) in men.
notes: The count is translated exactly as printed. vyāma = the span of the outstretched arms. Copula understood and supplied. "intestines" is the antecedent of tāni (line 75 (card 69)).

hindi: स्त्रियों में तीन व्याम के।
english: In women, three vyāmas.
notes: Elliptical: tāni (the intestines) and the copula are carried from line 76 (card 70) and are not supplied. The count is as printed.

hindi: रक्त के वायु से योग से अस्पष्ट शब्द कोलीयम्।
english: From the union of blood with Vāyu (wind, anila), the unclear word kolīyam.

text_flags.why: no safe correction: kolīyam is not a known word here; it presumably names an organ formed from blood and Vāyu, but its identity cannot be recovered (kola = jujube is only a guess about the root)

notes: The word kolīyam is unclear and is kept unsplit; no reading is adopted. Elliptical: the verb is carried from line 71 (card 65) and is not supplied. GROUPING: lines 71-78 (card 65/72) appear to be a continuing account of how the organs arise; this unit does not say what arises.

words.gloss: Kapha (śleṣman); blood; from the clear essence

hindi: हृदय फिर कफ और रक्त के प्रसाद यानी स्वच्छ सार से उत्पन्न होता है; वह कमल की कली के समान है, खोखला है और उसका मुख नीचे की ओर है।
english: The heart (hṛdaya), moreover, arises from the clear essence (prasāda) of Kapha and blood; it resembles a lotus bud (padmakośa), is hollow, and has its face downward.
notes: padmakośa = lotus bud (kośa also means sheath, calyx); the plainest sense "bud" is kept. adhomukha = "face downward", i.e. opening or point turned down; not interpreted further. Run-together: śleṣmaraktaprasādātsaṃbhavati, suṣiramadhomukhaṃ.

hindi: वह विशेष रूप से चेतना का स्थान है और चेतना के अनुगामी सब भावों का भी। उसके बाएँ पार्श्व में प्लीहा और फुप्फुस हैं, और दाहिनी ओर यकृत और क्लोम।
english: That (the heart) is especially the seat of consciousness (cetanā), and of all the states (bhāva) that follow consciousness. On its left side are the spleen (plīhan) and the lung (phupphusa), and on the right the liver (yakṛt) and the kloman.
notes: [02.05.80] tad = hṛdayam of line 79 (card 73). bhāva is rendered "states"; it may also mean "things, conditions". Copula understood and supplied. Run-together: tadviśeṣeṇa. [02.05.81] tasya = of the heart (line 79 (card 73)). kloman (klomam) is kept in the Sanskrit; its identity is disputed (variously the pancreas, the lung or the trachea region; no single equivalent is adopted). The placement of lung and organs is translated exactly as printed. Copula understood and supplied. Run-together: yakṛtklomaṃca.
lines_deva: तद्विशेषेण चेतनायाः स्थानं सर्वभावानां च चेतनानुगानां
तस्य वामपार्श्वे प्लीहा फुप्फुसश्च दक्षिणतो यकृत्क्लोमंच
lines_iast: tadviśeṣeṇa cetanāyāḥ sthānaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ ca cetanānugānāṃ
tasya vāmapārśve plīhā phupphusaśca dakṣiṇato yakṛtklomaṃca

hindi: इसी प्रकार कफ और रक्त को वहन करने वाले स्रोतसों और महाभूतों के प्रसाद यानी स्वच्छ सार से इन्द्रियाँ।
english: Likewise, from the clear essence (prasāda) of the srotas (channels) that carry Kapha and blood, and of the great elements (mahābhūta), the sense-organs (indriya).
notes: Elliptical: the verb (arise, as in line 79 (card 73)) is carried and is not supplied. Doctrinal terms srotas and mahābhūta are kept. The compound vāhinām agrees with srotasām.
lines_deva: तथा कफरक्तवाहिनां स्रोतसां महाभूतानां च प्रसादादिंद्रियाणि
lines_iast: tathā kapharaktavāhināṃ srotasāṃ mahābhūtānāṃ ca prasādādiṃdriyāṇi

words.gloss: white; circle (maṇḍala); probably the white of the eye

hindi: उनमें भी आँख में श्लेष्मा के प्रसाद यानी स्वच्छ सार से शुक्लमण्डल है, सम्भवतः आँख का सफेद भाग; वह पिता से उत्पन्न है।
english: Among these too, in the eye, from the clear essence of Kapha (śleṣman), the white circle (śukla-maṇḍala, probably the white of the eye); that is born from the father.
notes: netreśleṣmaṇaḥ is read as netre + śleṣmaṇaḥ ("in the eye, of Kapha"); the alternative netra-śleṣmaṇaḥ ("of the Kapha of the eye") gives nearly the same sense. śukla-maṇḍala = white circle; "probably the sclera" (probable). pitṛja = born from the father, as printed; not interpreted. Copula understood and supplied.

words.gloss: black; circle (maṇḍala); probably the dark part of the eye
sight; circle (maṇḍala); probably the pupil region

hindi: रक्त से कृष्णमण्डल है, सम्भवतः आँख का काला भाग; वह माता से उत्पन्न है। बीच में दृष्टिमण्डल है, सम्भवतः पुतली का क्षेत्र; वह दोनों के स्वभाव वाला है।
english: From blood, the black circle (kṛṣṇa-maṇḍala, probably the dark part of the eye); that is born from the mother. In the middle, the circle of sight (dṛṣṭi-maṇḍala, probably the pupil region); that has the nature of both.
notes: Elliptical: "arises" is carried from the previous units and not supplied. kṛṣṇa-maṇḍala and dṛṣṭi-maṇḍala: modern equivalents are probable only. "both" = presumably the father-born and mother-born, as the text does not say more. Copula understood and supplied.
lines_deva: असृजः कृष्णमंडलं तन्मातृजं मध्ये दृष्टिमंडलं तदुभयात्मकं
lines_iast: asṛjaḥ kṛṣṇamaṃḍalaṃ tanmātṛjaṃ madhye dṛṣṭimaṃḍalaṃ tadubhayātmakaṃ

words.gloss: eyelashes (pakṣma); eyelid (vartma); white; black; sight; named

hindi: पाँच मण्डल, अनुमानित पाठ पर, पक्ष्म यानी पलक के बाल, वर्त्म यानी पलक, शुक्ल, कृष्ण और दृष्टि नाम वाले हैं।
english: The five circles (maṇḍala), on a conjectural reading, are those named eyelashes (pakṣma), eyelid (vartma), white (śukla), black (kṛṣṇa) and sight (dṛṣṭi).

text_flags.why: possible: "āsyāni" (mouths) gives no sense and makes six items; five names are listed and ākhyāni "named" fits; kh -> s is a known OCR confusion in this print

notes: Copula understood and supplied. Without the correction the compound would add "mouths/faces" as a sixth item, contradicting "five".

hindi: उनकी सन्धियाँ चार हैं।
english: Their junctions (sandhi) are four.
notes: tat- refers to the five maṇḍalas of line 85 (card 78). Copula understood and supplied. Run-together: tatsaṃdhayaścatvāraḥ.

words.gloss: apāṅga (outer corner of the eye); kanīna (inner corner or pupil of the eye, probable)

hindi: और दो, अपांग यानी आँख के बाहरी कोने और कनीन यानी सम्भवतः आँख के भीतरी कोने में।
english: And two, at the apāṅga (outer corner of the eye) and the kanīna (probably the inner corner of the eye).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the preceding unit (86, outside this chunk), which presumably names the thing counted; the noun counted is not stated here and is not supplied. kanīna (cf. kanīnikā) is probably the inner corner or pupil of the eye; the exact sense is not firm. Case of the dual -nayoḥ taken as locative ('at'); genitive is possible.

hindi: इस प्रकार वे छह हैं।
english: Thus these are six.
notes: Copula understood. 'te' points back to the items counted in 86-87 (not named in this unit); GROUPING: appears to complete the count begun in 86-87.

hindi: और छह पटल यानी परतें।
english: And six paṭalas (layers).
notes: Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. paṭala = layer, coat (here of the eye, from the context of 87-94; the eye is not named in this line).

hindi: दो वर्त्म यानी पलकें।
english: Two vartmas (eyelids).
notes: Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. vartman = eyelid in the eye-section (standard); it also means 'path'.

hindi: बाहरी और अग्नि तथा जल पर आश्रित; दूसरा मांस, तीसरा मेद यानी चर्बी, चौथा अस्थि यानी हड्डी; उनकी मोटाई दृष्टि के पाँचवें अंश से है।
english: The outer one, and one resting on fire (agni) and water; the second, flesh; the third, fat (medas); the fourth, bone; their thickness is by a fifth part of sight (dṛṣṭi).

text_flags.why: possible: the full stop printed between the words stands for a space or a lost punctuation mark

notes: Elliptical and compressed: the noun (probably paṭala, 'layer', from 89) is not stated and is not supplied; 'their' (teṣām) is taken to refer to those unnamed items. The first part is hard: 'bāhyam ca āśritam agnyambhasī' is read as 'the outer one, and one resting on fire and water' (two descriptions of the first item, or two items); not settled. 'dvitīyam' is read with the series that follows (second: flesh, third: fat, fourth: bone). 'bahulatā' = thickness or abundance; 'dṛṣṭeḥ pañcamāṃśena' ('by a fifth part of sight') is kept literal and not interpreted. Print: 'cāśritamagnyaṃbhasīdvitīyaṃ' = ca āśritam agni-ambhasī dvitīyam (split is probable, not certain).
lines_deva: बाह्यं चाश्रितमग्न्यंभसीद्वितीयं मांसं.तृतीयं मेदश्चतुर्थमस्थि तेषां बहुलता दृष्टेः पंचमांशेन
lines_iast: bāhyaṃ cāśritamagnyaṃbhasīdvitīyaṃ māṃsaṃ.tṛtīyaṃ medaścaturthamasthi teṣāṃ bahulatā dṛṣṭeḥ paṃcamāṃśena

words.gloss: sirā (vein, vessel; standard); kaṇḍarā (large tendon; standard); fat (medas); Kapha; having the nature of

hindi: बन्धन के गुण यानी रज्जु तो चार हैं, जिनका स्वरूप सिरा यानी नस, कण्डरा यानी मोटा स्नायु-रज्जु, मेद और कफ है।
english: The binding strands (bandhana-guṇa), however, are four, having the nature of sirā (vein, vessel), kaṇḍarā (large tendon), fat (medas) and Kapha.
notes: guṇa is read as 'strand, cord' (that which binds); 'quality' is the other possible sense and is not adopted. sirā = vein or vessel (standard); kaṇḍarā = large tendon (standard). Kapha is capitalised as the doṣa. 'ātmaka' = having as its nature, consisting of.

hindi: श्लेष्मा यानी कफ तो सभी सन्धियों का परम बन्धन है, ऐसा पहले कहा गया।
english: Śleṣman (Kapha), however, is the highest binder of all joints; thus it was said before.
notes: The printed 'paraṃsarvasaṃdhibaṃdhanam' joins param and sarva (spacing slip, split without a flag). 'param' read as 'highest, chief'; 'further' is possible. The earlier statement is not located here. Copula understood.

hindi: आँख में आश्रित तेज तो अपने उद्गम बाहरी तेज के योग से कर्म के योग्य होता है, जैसे शस्त्र पत्थर से। अतियोग से वह क्षति पाता है।
english: The tejas (fire, radiance) resting in the eye becomes fit for its work through union with the outer tejas, its own source, as a weapon does with a stone; through excessive union it is harmed.

text_flags.why: possible: the visarga after bhavati looks like a misprinted danda; the two sentences run together

notes: Two sentences run together in the print (see text_flags); the first ends at 'bhavati'. 'svayoninā' is taken with bāhyatejasā ('its own source'). The stone (aśman) is probably a whetstone, but the Sanskrit only says 'stone'. karmaṇya = fit for work, functioning. The subject of 'upahanyate' (the tejas) is carried over.
lines_deva: नेत्राश्रितं तु तेजो बाह्यतेजसा स्वयोनिना योगाच्छस्त्रमिवाश्मना कर्मण्यं भवतिःअतियोगादुपहन्यते
lines_iast: netrāśritaṃ tu tejo bāhyatejasā svayoninā yogācchastramivāśmanā karmaṇyaṃ bhavatiḥatiyogādupahanyate

hindi: और वह बिजली की तरह और वड़वामुख यानी समुद्र की भीतरी अग्नि की तरह जल के मध्य में स्थित होकर भी वीर्य यानी शक्ति की प्रबलता से अपने तेजत्व को नहीं छोड़ता।
english: And that (tejas), like lightning and like the vaḍavāmukha (the submarine fire), even when situated in the midst of water, does not abandon its fiery nature (tejastva) because of the excellence of its vīrya (potency).
notes: 'tat' is taken as the tejas of 94. vaḍavāmukha = the fire of the mare's mouth, said to burn under the ocean (standard in Sanskrit literature). Print: 'vīryyotkarṣāt' has doubled y (print habit, normalised once). 'vaidyutavat' = 'like the lightning (fire)'.

words.gloss: flesh; blood; Kapha; fat; clear essence

hindi: मांस, रक्त और कफ के प्रसाद यानी सार अंश से तो जिह्वा उत्पन्न होती है। मांस, रक्त, कफ और मेद के प्रसाद यानी सार अंश से दो वृषण यानी अण्डकोश के गोलक।
english: From the clear essence (prasāda) of flesh, blood and Kapha, however, the tongue (jihvā) arises. From the clear essence (prasāda) of flesh, blood, Kapha and fat, the two testes (vṛṣaṇa).

text_flags.why: near certain: standard spelling is jihvā; hv/vh letter reversal in this print, normalised in `w` (also in line 104 (card 96))

notes: [02.05.96] prasāda = clear, pure part (the finest part); the word is kept literal. asṛk = blood. The same letter reversal jivhā occurs in line 104 (card 96) and is normalised there without a new flag. [02.05.97] Elliptical: the verb 'arise' (jāyete) is carried from 96 and is not supplied. The closing 'iti' marks the end of the statement and is not translated.

words.gloss: tongue; binding (the binding of the tongue; sense uncertain)

hindi: प्राण के दस आयतन यानी आश्रय स्थान हैं: मूर्धा यानी सिर, जिह्वाबन्धन यानी जीभ का बन्धन, कण्ठ, हृदय, नाभि, बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय, गूद यानी गुदा, शुक्र यानी वीर्य, ओज और रक्त।
english: There are ten seats of life (prāṇāyatana): the head (mūrdhan), the jihvābandhana (tongue-binding), the throat, the heart (hṛdaya), the navel, the bladder (basti), the gūda (anus, rectum), śukra (semen), ojas and blood.
notes: Ten items are named: head, tongue-binding, throat, heart, navel, bladder, gūda, śukra, ojas, blood. 'jihvābandhana' is kept literal ('tongue-binding'); it may mean the root of the tongue or the frenulum, which is not settled. 'kaṇṭha' may mean neck or throat. basti = bladder here (standard); gūda = anus or rectum. Print: 'mūrddhā' has doubled d (normalised to mūrdhā, a print habit). ojas is a doctrinal term and is not forced into a modern equivalent.
lines_deva: दश प्राणायतनानि मूर्द्धा जिह्वाबंधनं कंठो हृदयं नाभिर्बस्तिर्गूदः शुक्रमोजो रक्तं
lines_iast: daśa prāṇāyatanāni mūrddhā jihvābaṃdhanaṃ kaṃṭho hṛdayaṃ nābhirbastirgūdaḥ śukramojo raktaṃ

hindi: इनमें से पहले सात फिर महामर्म नाम वाले हैं।
english: Of these, the first seven, again, are named mahāmarma (great marma, vital point).
notes: 'The first seven' are, in the order of 98, head, tongue-binding, throat, heart, navel, bladder, gūda (the order is the reader's inference from 98). Copula understood. marma is a doctrinal term (a vital point of the body) and is kept.

hindi: सोलह कण्डराएँ हैं; उनमें से हाथों और पैरों में दो-दो, गर्दन और पीठ में चार, अलग-अलग।
english: There are sixteen kaṇḍarās (large tendons); of them, two each in the hands and feet, four, separately, in the neck and the back.
notes: Copula understood. 'dve dve' is distributive ('two each'). Taken together the numbers make sixteen only if 'four' belongs to each of neck and back (8 + 4 + 4); the Sanskrit says only 'four, separately' and no 'each' is added. Counts are translated as printed.
lines_deva: षोडश कंडराः तासां द्वे द्वे करचरणेषु चतस्रः पृथकग्रीवापृष्ठयोः
lines_iast: ṣoḍaśa kaṃḍarāḥ tāsāṃ dve dve karacaraṇeṣu catasraḥ pṛthakagrīvāpṛṣṭhayoḥ

words.gloss: flesh; vessel; snāyu (ligament, sinew); bone; born of

hindi: सोलह जाल हैं; उनमें मांस, सिरा, स्नायु और अस्थि से उत्पन्न, एक-एक स्थान पर चार, गुल्फ यानी टखने और मणिबन्ध यानी कलाई में, परस्पर झरोखेदार स्थित हैं।
english: There are sixteen jālas (nets); of them, those born of flesh, vessel, snāyu (ligament) and bone, four in each single place, at the ankle (gulpha) and the wrist (maṇibandha), are situated mutually latticed.
notes: jāla = net, mesh (a doctrinal structure; no firm modern equivalent). The four kinds (flesh, vessel, snāyu, bone) are read as the four per site; with four sites (two ankles, two wrists) the total is sixteen, but that sum is not stated. 'gavākṣita' = made like a window (gavākṣa, lattice), i.e. interlaced; the sense is kept literal. 'gulpha' = ankle, 'maṇibandha' = wrist (both standard). 'ca' joins the two sites.
lines_deva: षोडश जालानि तेषां मांससिरास्नाय्वस्थिजानि चत्वार्य्येकैकत्र गुल्फे मणिबंधे च परस्परगवाक्षितानि स्थितानि
lines_iast: ṣoḍaśa jālāni teṣāṃ māṃsasirāsnāyvasthijāni catvāryyekaikatra gulphe maṇibaṃdhe ca parasparagavākṣitāni sthitāni

hindi: छह कूर्च हैं: हाथों, पैरों, गर्दन और मेढ्र यानी शिश्न में।
english: Six kūrcas (bundles, sense uncertain): in the hands, feet, neck and penis (meḍhra).
notes: Elliptical: copula understood and not supplied. kūrca = tuft, bundle (as a body part it is not firmly identified; the same word names a part of the foot in 111). The line does not say how the six are shared among the places. Print: doubled cc in 'kūrccā' is a print habit (normalised).

words.gloss: peśī (muscle); binding; for the purpose of
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, loc. sg. used as ind.

hindi: चार मांसरज्जु हैं, पृष्ठवंश यानी रीढ़ के दोनों ओर, पेशियों को बाँधने के लिए; उनमें दो बाहरी और दो भीतर स्थित।
english: There are four flesh-cords (māṃsarajju) on both sides of the spine (pṛṣṭhavaṃśa), for the binding of the peśīs (muscles); of them two are outer and two are situated inside.
notes: Copula understood. peśī = muscle (standard). The cords are on both sides of the spine; the text does not say how many on each side. 'pṛṣṭhavaṃśam ubhayataḥ' takes the accusative with ubhayataḥ.
lines_deva: चतस्रो मांसरज्जवः पृष्ठवंशमुभयतः पेशीनिबंधनार्थे तासां द्वे बाह्ये द्वे चाभ्यंतरस्थिते
lines_iast: catasro māṃsarajjavaḥ pṛṣṭhavaṃśamubhayataḥ peśīnibaṃdhanārthe tāsāṃ dve bāhye dve cābhyaṃtarasthite

hindi: सात सीवनी यानी सिलाई की रेखाएँ हैं; उनमें पाँच सिर में, जीभ और मेहन यानी शिश्न में एक-एक।
english: There are seven sīvanīs (seams, probably sutures); of them five are in the head, one each in the tongue and the penis (mehana).

text_flags.why: near certain: jivhā is the hv/vh letter reversal for jihvā (also at 96); normalised in `w`

notes: sīvanī = sevanī, seam; 'suture' is the usual modern reading (probable). The count 5 + 1 + 1 = seven matches. Print: 'jivhā' for jihvā (letter reversal, normalised; flagged at 96). Copula understood.
lines_deva: सप्त सीवन्यः ताः पंच शिरसि जिव्हामेहनयोरेकैका
lines_iast: sapta sīvanyaḥ tāḥ paṃca śirasi jivhāmehanayorekaikā

words.gloss: to be avoided, to be spared

hindi: और शस्त्र से परिहार्य यानी बचाने योग्य।
english: And to be avoided with the śastra (blade, surgical instrument).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 104 (the subject, presumably the sīvanīs, is not stated in this unit and is not supplied). parihārya = to be avoided; the sense 'to be spared from the cut' is the natural one. Print: doubled y in 'parihāryyāḥ' normalised.

words.gloss: ankle; knee; groin; wrist; elbow; armpit

hindi: चौदह अस्थि-संघात यानी हड्डियों के समूह हैं; उनमें से एक-एक गुल्फ यानी टखने, जानु यानी घुटने, वंक्षण यानी जाँघ और पेट के बीच के भाग, मणिबन्ध यानी कलाई, कूर्पर यानी कोहनी और कक्षा यानी बगल में तथा, अनुमानित पाठ पर, त्रिक यानी सम्भवतः त्रिकास्थि वाले क्षेत्र और सिर में।
english: There are fourteen asthi-saṃghātas (bone assemblages); of them one each in the ankle, knee, groin, wrist, elbow and armpit, and, on a conjectural reading, in the trika (probably the sacral region) and the head.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ja' looks like an inserted syllable; without it the places are twelve limb joints (6 sites on two sides) plus trika and head, which makes fourteen

notes: The sum 12 + 1 + 1 = 14 fits the flagged reading; this arithmetic is the evidence, not stated in the text. The translation adopts the corrected reading and is hedged ('on a conjectural reading'). 'trika' = the lower-back region (sacral, probable). 'ekaikaḥ' is taken as 'one each' (one at each of the paired places). Copula understood.

words.gloss: sīmantas (partings; here probably sutures of bone)

hindi: उसी प्रकार सीमन्त यानी सम्भवतः अस्थियों की सीवन-रेखाएँ; वे तो पाँच सिर में, इस प्रकार अठारह।
english: Likewise the sīmantas (probably sutures of bones); they, however, are five in the head: thus eighteen.
notes: Elliptical: copula understood. 'Likewise' refers to the places listed in 106, and eighteen is probably twelve limb places + trika + five in the head (a reading, not stated). 'sīmanta' = hair-parting; as a bone term, a suture (probable). Printed 'śirasītyaṣṭādaśa' = śirasi iti aṣṭādaśa.

hindi: तीन सौ अस्थियाँ साठ से अधिक, यानी तीन सौ साठ।
english: Three hundred bones, in excess by sixty (that is, three hundred and sixty).
notes: Count translated as printed: 300 plus 60 = 360. Printed 'ṣaṣṭhyā'dhikāni': the avagraha after -ā is a print habit (no flag).

words.gloss: forty; hundred (that is, one hundred and forty)

hindi: और उनमें से एक सौ चालीस शाखाओं यानी हाथ-पैरों में, एक सौ बीस अन्तराधि यानी सम्भवतः धड़ में, सौ सिर में।
english: And of them, a hundred and forty in the limbs (śākhā), a hundred and twenty in the antarādhi (probably the trunk), a hundred in the head.

text_flags.why: near certain: the initial ca- is lost; 'catvāriṃśat-śatam' is the number 140 and the three parts then add to 360 as in 108
possible: the final m of śatam is printed at the head of the next word (spacing slip)

notes: 140 + 120 + 100 = 360, matching 108 (arithmetic given as evidence for the flags). Words restored: sa-viṃśa-śatam (sa = 'with', so 'a hundred with twenty') and antarādhau; the print has 'sa' separate and the m misplaced. antarādhi = trunk, the middle of the body (probable). Printed 'mūrddhnīti' = mūrdhni iti.
lines_deva: तेषां च त्वारिंशच्छतं शाखासु स विंशशत मंतराधौ शतं मूर्द्ध्नीति
lines_iast: teṣāṃ ca tvāriṃśacchataṃ śākhāsu sa viṃśaśata maṃtarādhau śataṃ mūrddhnīti

words.gloss: first part of ekaika-, 'each single' (print split)
second part of ekaikasmin, 'in each single' (print split)

hindi: वहाँ एक-एक सक्थि यानी निचले अंग में पाँच पादनख, प्रत्येक अंगुली में तीन अस्थियाँ, वे पन्द्रह।
english: There, in each single lower limb (sakthi): five foot-nails (pādanakha); in each toe three bones; those are fifteen.

text_flags.why: possible: the words are split wrongly in the print (ekaikasmin) and carry a stray final -a

notes: Reading: tatra ekaikasmin sakthini; the print splits ekaikasmin over two tokens, so the first half is given to the first token and the second half to 'kasmina'. 'sakthi' = thigh or whole leg; here the lower limb. 'tāni pañcadaśa' ('those are fifteen') is taken as the three bones of each of five toes (3 x 5); the Sanskrit does not say which items it counts. The nails are counted among the bones as printed. 'nakhāḥpratyekam' is run together in the print (split without a flag).
lines_deva: तत्रैकै कस्मिन सक्थिनि पंच पादनखाःप्रत्येकमंगुल्यां त्रीण्यस्थीनि तानि पंचदश
lines_iast: tatraikai kasmina sakthini paṃca pādanakhāḥpratyekamaṃgulyāṃ trīṇyasthīni tāni paṃcadaśa

words.gloss: kūrca (a part of the foot; sense uncertain); ankle; shank
heel (on a conjectural reading); knee; thigh

hindi: पाँच पादशलाकाएँ, उनका एक प्रतिबन्धक, कूर्च, गुल्फ यानी टखने और जङ्घा यानी घुटने से नीचे के भाग में दो-दो, तथा, अनुमानित पाठ पर, एड़ी, जानु और ऊरु में एक-एक।
english: Five foot-rods (pādaśalākā); one binder of them; two each in the kūrca, ankle (gulpha) and shank (jaṅghā); and, on a conjectural reading, one each in the heel, knee (jānu) and thigh (ūru).

text_flags.why: possible: pāṇi (hand) does not suit the leg, and the compound would not have visarga/r; pārṣṇi (heel) fits the list of leg places

notes: Continues the count of the leg begun in 110: 5 nails + 15 toe-bones + 5 rods + 1 binder + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 35, which is a quarter of the 140 in 109 (arithmetic as evidence only). 'śalākā' = rod, splint; 'kūrca' is kept untranslated (sense uncertain). The printed 'pāṇi' is the word for hand; the heel reading is hedged. Print: doubled cc in 'kūrcca' normalised. 'tat' in tatpratibandhaka is taken to refer to the rods.
lines_deva: पंचपादशलाकाः तत्प्रतिबंधकमेकं द्वे द्वे कूर्च्चगुल्फजंघास्वेकैकं पाणिर्जानूरुषु
lines_iast: paṃcapādaśalākāḥ tatpratibaṃdhakamekaṃ dve dve kūrccagulphajaṃghāsvekaikaṃ pāṇirjānūruṣu

hindi: और नख-अस्थि आदि सभी, सक्थि के समान, दोनों बाहुओं में भी।
english: And all, beginning with the nail-bones, as in the lower limb, also in the two arms.
notes: Elliptical: copula understood. Printed 'sarvāṇica' = sarvāṇi ca and 'sakthivadvāhvośca' = sakthi-vat bāhvoḥ ca (v/b interchange is common in the print, 'vāhvoḥ' for bāhvoḥ normalised). 'nakhāsthyādīni' is taken as 'beginning with nail(-bone)s', as in 110.

hindi: चौबीस पर्शुकाएँ यानी पसलियाँ।
english: Twenty-four parśukās (ribs).
notes: Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. Counts as printed (24); the line does not say whether it is per side or in all.

hindi: उतने ही उनके स्थालक यानी छोटी थालियाँ और अर्बुद यानी उभार हैं।
english: Just as many are their sthālakas (small dishes) and arbudas (lumps).
notes: Copula understood. 'their' (tat-) refers to the ribs of 113. sthālaka and arbuda are not firmly identified in modern anatomy (probably the cup-like and knob-like articulating ends of the ribs, a guess, not stated). arbuda elsewhere means tumour; here 'lump' is kept literal.

hindi: तीस पीठ में।
english: Thirty in the back.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the bone count of 108-114; the thing counted (bones) is not stated in the line and is not supplied. Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood.

hindi: आठ छाती में।
english: Eight in the chest.
notes: Printed 'aṣṭāvurasi' = aṣṭau urasi. GROUPING: appears to continue the bone count of 108-114; the thing counted (bones) is not stated in the line and is not supplied. Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood.

words.gloss: in the bhaga (pubic or pudendal region, probable)

hindi: एक-एक भग यानी सम्भवतः जघन-क्षेत्र में और त्रिक यानी सम्भवतः त्रिकास्थि वाले क्षेत्र में।
english: One each in the bhaga (probably the pubic region) and the trika (probably the sacral region).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the bone count of 108-114; the thing counted (bones) is not stated in the line and is not supplied. Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. bhaga usually means the female genitals; as a place for a bone it is read as the pubic region, which is probable but not certain. trika as in 106.

words.gloss: in the two hips or buttocks (nitamba; standard)

hindi: और दोनों नितम्बों में दो।
english: And two in the two nitambas (hips).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the bone count of 108-114; the thing counted (bones) is not stated in the line and is not supplied. Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. Whether 'two' is the total or per side is not stated.

hindi: उसी प्रकार, अनुमानित पाठ पर, अक्षक यानी सम्भवतः हँसली, अंस यानी कन्धे और अंसफलक यानी कन्धे की चपटी हड्डियों में।
english: Likewise, on a conjectural reading, in the akṣaka (probably the collarbone), the shoulder (aṃsa) and the shoulder-blades (aṃsaphalaka).

text_flags.why: possible: printed 'kaṃsāṃsa' looks like a slip for kāṃsāṃsa (akṣaka + aṃsa + aṃsaphalaka); the book's own form could also be read akṣa-kaṃsa; sense not firm

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the bone count of 108-114; the thing counted (bones) is not stated in the line and is not supplied. Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. 'Likewise' means 'in the same number as in 118'; the number is not repeated and is not supplied. The reading of the compound is uncertain (see text_flags); aṃsaphalaka = shoulder-blade (scapula, standard).

words.gloss: jatru (probably the region of the collarbone and root of the neck); palate (tālu)

hindi: वैसे ही गण्ड यानी गाल, कर्ण यानी कान और शंख यानी कनपटी में, तथा जत्रु यानी सम्भवतः हँसली वाला स्थान और तालु में।
english: Likewise in the cheeks (gaṇḍa), ears and temples (śaṅkha), and in the jatru (probably the region of the collarbone) and the palate (tālu).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the bone count of 108-114; the thing counted (bones) is not stated in the line and is not supplied. Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. 'Likewise' repeats the number of 118/119, not restated. jatru = collarbone or the region where the neck meets the shoulder (probable). śaṅkha = temple (also 'conch').

hindi: तेरह गर्दन में, चार कण्ठनाड़ी यानी सम्भवतः श्वासनली में, दो हनुबन्धन यानी जबड़े के जोड़ों में; बत्तीस दाँत और उसी प्रकार उलूखल यानी सम्भवतः दाँतों के गड्ढे; तीन नाक में, छह सिर में।
english: Thirteen in the neck; four in the kaṇṭhanāḍī (probably the windpipe), two in the jaw-joints (hanubandhana); thirty-two teeth, and likewise ulūkhalas (probably tooth-sockets); three in the nose, six in the head.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the bone count of 108-114; the thing counted (bones) is not stated in the line and is not supplied. Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied; the copula is understood. 'tadvat' means 'as many' (thirty-two sockets for thirty-two teeth); the number is not repeated. ulūkhala = mortar; as the socket of a tooth it is probable. Print: 'kaṃṭhanāḍyāṃdve' joins two words (kaṇṭhanāḍyām dve; split without a flag). 'hanubandhane' is taken as the two jaw-joints (dual).
lines_deva: त्रयोदश ग्रीवायां चत्वारि कंठनाड्यांद्वे हनुबंधने द्वात्रिंशद्दंताः तद्वदुलूखलानि च त्रीणि नासायां षट् शिरसि
lines_iast: trayodaśa grīvāyāṃ catvāri kaṃṭhanāḍyāṃdve hanubaṃdhane dvātriṃśaddaṃtāḥ tadvadulūkhalāni ca trīṇi nāsāyāṃ ṣaṭ śirasi

words.gloss: knee; hip; shoulder; cheek; palate; temple; groin; middle; head

hindi: वे जानु, नितम्ब, अंस, गण्ड, तालु, शंख, वंक्षण, मध्य और सिरों में कपाल नाम वाले हैं।
english: Those in the knees, hips, shoulders, cheeks, palate, temples, groin, middle and heads are named kapāla (plates).
notes: 'tāni' refers to the bones counted in 115-121 at these places. The list is a locative dvandva; 'madhya' (middle) is kept as printed with no further sense, and the divisions 'vaṅkṣaṇamadhya' (middle of the groin) are possible. kapāla = potsherd, plate, also skull; here the name of one class of bone (see 127). Copula understood.

hindi: दाँत तो रुचक हैं।
english: The teeth (daśana), however, are rucakas.
notes: Copula understood. rucaka is one of the classes of bone (see 127) and is kept untranslated.

words.gloss: nose; ear; neck; eye; sheath, socket
taruṇas (tender ones; the taruṇa bones are usually taken as cartilage, probable)

hindi: घ्राण यानी नाक, कर्ण यानी कान, ग्रीवा यानी गर्दन और अक्षिकोश यानी आँख के गड्ढों में तरुण यानी कोमल हैं, जो सम्भवतः उपास्थि हैं। पाणि यानी हाथ, पाद यानी पैर, पार्श्व यानी बगल और पृष्ठ यानी पीठ में वलय यानी छल्ले हैं।
english: In the nose, ears, neck and eye-sockets (akṣikoṣa) are the taruṇas (tender ones, usually taken as cartilage, probable). In the hands, feet, sides and back are the valayas (rings).
notes: [02.05.124] Copula understood. The printed 'grīvā'kṣi' has an avagraha after -ā (print habit, no flag). 'taruṇa' = young, tender; the modern identification as cartilage is probable. akṣikoṣa = eye-sheath, taken as eye-socket (probable). [02.05.125] Copula understood. 'valaya' = ring; the class of bone is named after its shape, and no further explanation is added. (The Hindi 'छल्ले जैसी हड्डियाँ' only restates the name valaya, rings.)

hindi: शेष नलक यानी नलियाँ हैं।
english: The remaining ones are nalakas (tubes).
notes: Copula understood. The closing 'iti' marks the end of the classification and is not translated. nalaka = a small tube or reed; the class of tubular bones is the usual reading (probable).

hindi: नाम के अनुसार चलने वाली ये पाँच प्रकार की अस्थियाँ हैं, अनुमानित पाठ पर। क्योंकि उनमें सिराओं और स्नायुओं से मांस बँधे हुए हैं।
english: These are five kinds of bones, following their names, on a conjectural reading. For in them the fleshes (masses of flesh) are bound by vessels (sirā) and snāyus (ligaments).

text_flags.why: possible: 'amūnīni' is not a word; nāmānugatāni + amūni with the sandhi -ny a- is the likely sense, and the five classes of 123-126 (kapāla, rucaka, taruṇa, valaya, nalaka) fit

notes: [02.05.127] The five classes are kapāla (122), rucaka (123), taruṇa (124), valaya (125), nalaka (126) (the list is inferred from those units). 'following their names' = the name matches the nature of each class. Copula understood. [02.05.128] 'teṣu' refers to the bones. The plural māṃsāni is kept as 'fleshes' (flesh-masses, perhaps muscles); no word is added. sirā = vein or vessel; snāyu = ligament, sinew (both standard).
lines_deva: तेषु हि सिराभिः स्नायुभिश्च निबद्धानि मांसानि
lines_iast: teṣu hi sirābhiḥ snāyubhiśca nibaddhāni māṃsāni

hindi: अस्थि-सन्धियों के दो सौ, दस अधिक, यानी दो सौ दस।
english: Two hundred, in excess by ten (that is, two hundred and ten), of the joints of bones (asthi-sandhi).
notes: Count as printed: 200 plus 10 = 210. Elliptical: no verb; the line states a number of joints and 'number' is not in the Sanskrit (the Hindi 'संख्या' is the natural gloss of the genitive and adds only that). Copula understood.

hindi: उनमें से अड़सठ शाखाओं यानी हाथ-पैरों में।
english: Of them, sixty-eight in the limbs (śākhā).
notes: GROUPING: lines 130-132 (card 120/122) appear to form one statement continuing line 129 (card 119) (the total of 210 asthisaṃdhi): 'of them 68 in the limbs, 59 in the trunk, 80 above'. Elliptical: no verb, and the counted noun is unstated; from 129 it is probably the bone-joints (asthisaṃdhi). teṣām = of those 210. śākhā = the limbs, i.e. arms and legs (standard). Numbers are translated as printed. The visarga before ś (-ḥśā-) is regular.

hindi: उनसठ अन्तराधि यानी धड़ में।
english: Fifty-nine in the trunk (antarādhi).
notes: Elliptical as in 130. antarādhi = the trunk, the middle part of the body (standard). ekona-ṣaṣṭi = sixty minus one.

hindi: अस्सी ऊपर।
english: Eighty above (ūrdhvam).

text_flags.why: possible: the sites listed in lines 139-145 (card 129/134) add up to 83 (8+3+18+32+3+12+2+5) and 68+59+83 = 210, the total of line 129 (card 119); as printed 68+59+80 = 207. The translation keeps the printed 'eighty' and the word list keeps aśītiḥ.

notes: Elliptical as in 130-131. ūrdhvam = above, probably the region above the trunk (neck and head) (probable); the text does not say more. The print divides 'aśītir ūrdhvam' as 'aśīti rūrdhvaṃ' (the r of aśītir attached to the next word): regular sandhi, words restored. The three totals as printed (68 + 59 + 80) make 207, not the 210 of line 129 (card 119); see text_flags. The translation keeps 'eighty' as printed.

hindi: वहाँ प्रत्येक सक्थि यानी सम्भवतः शाखा में, पैर की प्रत्येक उँगली में तीन, अँगूठे में दो।
english: There, in each single sakthi (probably meaning limb), three in each toe (pādāṅguli), two in the great toe (aṅguṣṭha).

text_flags.why: possible: the locative of the neuter sakthi is sakthni (or sakthini); the printed bare 'sakthi' also stands in line 160 (card 148), so it may be an edition habit

notes: GROUPING: lines 133-134 (card 123/124) appear to belong together ('those are fourteen' totals this line). sakthi literally means thigh or leg; here it is read as each of the four limbs (śākhā), since 68 = 4 x 17 (14 + ankle + knee + groin) (probable). aṅgulau is the optional -au locative of the feminine aṅguli; used distributively with pratyekam ('in each toe'). aṅguṣṭha = thumb or great toe; the foot is being counted, so great toe. The counted noun is unstated (probably the bone-joints, from 129). The printed locative 'sakthi' is the same in line 160 (card 148); see text_flags.
lines_deva: तत्रैकैकस्मिन् सक्थि पादांगुलौ प्रत्येकं त्रयः द्वावंगुष्ठे
lines_iast: tatraikaikasmin sakthi pādāṃgulau pratyekaṃ trayaḥ dvāvaṃguṣṭhe

hindi: वे चौदह हैं।
english: Those are fourteen.
notes: Copula understood and supplied (a plain nominal sentence). Check: 3 x 4 toes + 2 = 14 in the foot, as printed in 133.

hindi: टखने, घुटने और वंक्षण यानी जाँघ के मूल में एक-एक; अनुमानित पाठ पर कमर के कपालों में तीन।
english: One each in the ankles (gulpha), knees (jānu) and groins (vaṅkṣaṇa); three in the hip kapālas (kaṭikapāla, on a conjectural reading).

text_flags.why: possible: 'kati' (how many) gives no sense here; kaṭi-kapāla (hip bone-plate) fits the trunk count; the same spelling stands in line 150 (card 138)

notes: gulpha = ankle, jānu = knee, vaṅkṣaṇa = groin (all standard). kapāla = literally skull or bone-plate; in this passage the name of a class of flat bones (see 122) (probable). Limb check: 14 (toes) + ankle + knee + groin = 17 per limb, x 4 = 68, matching 130. The counted noun is unstated.

hindi: चौबीस पृष्ठवंश यानी रीढ़ में।
english: Twenty-four in the spine (pṛṣṭhavaṃśa).
notes: pṛṣṭhavaṃśa = literally back-ridge, the spine (standard).

hindi: वैसे ही दोनों पार्श्वों यानी बगलों में।
english: Likewise in the two flanks (pārśva).
notes: tadvat = 'like that', i.e. like the preceding count (presumably the same number as in 136); the translation does not supply the number. pārśva = the side of the body (standard).

hindi: आठ उरस् यानी छाती में।
english: Eight in the chest (uras).
notes: Trunk check: 3 (135) + 24 (136) + 'tadvat' for the flanks (137, presumably 24) + 8 = 59, matching 131.

hindi: आठ ग्रीवा यानी गर्दन में।
english: Eight in the neck (grīvā).

hindi: तीन कण्ठनाड़ी में, जो सम्भवतः श्वासनली है।
english: Three in the kaṇṭhanāḍī (probably the windpipe).
notes: kaṇṭhanāḍī = throat-channel, probably the windpipe (probable; the gullet is the alternative).

hindi: अठारह, कण्ठनाड़ी से बँधे हुए, हृदय, यकृत, क्लोम जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, और नाड़ियों में।
english: Eighteen, bound to the kaṇṭhanāḍī, in the heart (hṛdaya), liver (yakṛt), kloma (an organ of disputed identity) and channels (nāḍī).

text_flags.why: possible: nibaddhā (f. sg.) cannot agree with the plural 'aṣṭādaśa'; a dropped visarga gives nibaddhāḥ

notes: hṛdaya = heart and yakṛt = liver (standard); kloma = an organ near the heart and liver, identity disputed (lung, pancreas and others are proposed). The last compound is read as a plain dvandva of four members; the alternative is 'in the nāḍīs of heart, liver and kloma'. The printed 'nibaddhā' does not agree with the plural numeral; the plural masculine is read (see text_flags).

hindi: बत्तीस दाँतों की जड़ों में।
english: Thirty-two in the tooth-roots (dantamūla).

words.gloss: kākala (throat part, identity disputed); nose; head

hindi: एक-एक काकल यानी गले के एक भाग जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, नाक और मूर्धा यानी सिर में।
english: One each in the kākala (a throat part of disputed identity), the nose (nāsā) and the head (mūrdhan).
notes: kākala: identity disputed (the uvula or the larynx prominence have been proposed). mūrdhan = head or crown. Print: 'mūrddhasu' has a doubled dh after r, normalised to mūrdhasu (orthographic, recorded once).

words.gloss: cheek; ear; temple; eyelid; eye; jaw; joints
words.gram: dvandva then tat-puruṣa, m. loc. pl.

hindi: गाल, कान, कनपटी, पलक, आँख और जबड़े के जोड़ों में दो-दो। दोनों भौंहों के ऊपर दो; सिर के कपालों में पाँच।
english: Two each in the joints (saṃdhi) of the cheek (gaṇḍa), ear (karṇa), temple (śaṅkha), eyelid (vartman), eye (netra) and jaw (hanu). Two above the two eyebrows (bhrū); five in the kapālas of the head (śiras).
notes: [02.05.144] gaṇḍa = cheek, śaṅkha = temple, vartma = eyelid (standard). saṃdhi stands last in the compound and is read as governing all six members. dvau dvau = two each. [02.05.145] Upper-region check: neck 8 (139) + 3 (140) + 18 (141) + 32 (142) + 3 (143) + 12 (144) + 2 + 5 (145) = 83, not the 80 of line 132 (card 122) (see the flag there).

words.gloss: finger or toe (conjectural); ankle; knee; wrist; elbow

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर उँगलियों, टखनों, घुटनों, मणिबन्ध यानी कलाई और कुहनियों में कोर यानी कली नामक। काँख, वंक्षण और दाँतों की जड़ों में उलूखल यानी ओखली नामक।
english: In the fingers or toes (aṅguli, on a conjectural reading), ankles, knees, wrists (maṇibandha) and elbows (kūrpara): (ones) named kora (bud). In the armpits (kakṣā), groins (vaṅkṣaṇa) and tooth-roots (dantamūla): (ones) named ulūkhala (mortar).

text_flags.why: possible: 'meṃguli' is not a word; aṅguli (finger, toe) fits the list of limb sites (finger, ankle, knee, wrist, elbow) and a misreading of a- as me- is plausible

notes: [02.05.146] maṇibandha = wrist, kūrpara = elbow (standard). kora = a bud. Elliptical: the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'; from the context these are kinds of bone-joint (see 154). The first member is a conjectured reading (see text_flags). [02.05.147] kakṣā = armpit (standard). Elliptical: unstated noun shown as '(ones)'. The ū-ū of -mūleṣūlū- is regular sandhi (mūleṣu + ulūkhala).

words.gloss: shoulder; seat; anus; bhaga (female genital organ); hip (conjectural)

hindi: अंसपीठ यानी सम्भवतः कन्धे के फलक वाला भाग, गुदा, भग यानी स्त्री के जननांग और अनुमानित पाठ पर नितम्बों में सामुद्ग यानी डिब्बी के प्रकार के।
english: In the shoulder-seats (aṃsapīṭha, probably the region of the shoulder-blade), anus (guda), bhaga (the female genital organ) and hips (nitamba, on a conjectural reading): (ones) of the sāmudga (casket) kind.

text_flags.why: possible: 'titaṃba' is not a word; nitamba (hip) fits the sites (cf. 118, 122) and na/ta is a common misreading; 'gudbhaga' probably dropped the a of guda (sense unchanged)

notes: aṃsapīṭha = seat of the shoulder, probably the shoulder-blade region (probable). guda = anus, bhaga = vulva (standard), nitamba = hip or buttock (standard). sāmudga is from samudga, a casket or lidded box. Elliptical: unstated noun shown as '(ones)'. The printed 'gudbhaga' reads as guda-bhaga.

hindi: ग्रीवा और पृष्ठवंश यानी रीढ़ में प्रतर।
english: In the neck and the spine: pratara (ones).
notes: pratara is the name of a kind of joint; its literal sense is left untranslated. Elliptical: unstated noun shown as '(ones)'.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर सिर और कमर के कपालों में तुन्नसेवनी नामक, यह नाम भी अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: In the head and hip kapālas (on a conjectural reading): (ones) named tunnasevanī (also on a conjectural reading; sevanī means a seam).

text_flags.why: possible: as in line 135 (card 125), kaṭi-kapāla (hip bone-plate) fits; 'kati' gives no sense
possible: tūna is not a known word; the known name is tunnasevanī

notes: Two conjectured readings (see text_flags). sevanī = a seam, suture. Elliptical: unstated noun shown as '(ones)'.

hindi: दोनों जबड़ों के दोनों ओर वायसतुण्ड यानी कौए की चोंच।
english: On both sides of the two jaws (hanu): vāyasatuṇḍa (crow-beak) (ones).
notes: hanū is the accusative dual governed by ubhayataḥ ('on both sides of'), a regular construction, so nothing is emended. Elliptical: unstated noun shown as '(ones)'.

words.gloss: throat; eye; heart; liver; kloma (identity disputed); channels

hindi: कण्ठ, आँखों, हृदय, यकृत, क्लोम जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, और नाड़ियों में मण्डल यानी गोल घेरा नामक।
english: In the throat (kaṇṭha), eyes (netra), heart, liver, kloma (an organ of disputed identity) and channels (nāḍī): (ones) named maṇḍala (circle).
notes: Read as a plain dvandva of six members; the alternative is 'in the nāḍīs of throat, eyes, heart, liver and kloma' (compare 141). Elliptical: unstated noun shown as '(ones)'.

words.gloss: ear; śṛṅgāṭaka (a named site in the head)

hindi: श्रोत्र और शृंगाटकों में शंखावर्त यानी शंख की भँवर।
english: In the ears (śrotra) and the śṛṅgāṭakas: śaṅkhāvarta (conch-whorl) (ones).
notes: śṛṅgāṭaka is the name of a site in the head (a marma); no modern equivalent is forced. Print: 'barttāḥ' normalised to vartāḥ (b/v interchange and doubled -rtt-, recorded once). Elliptical: unstated noun shown as '(ones)'.

hindi: अस्थिसन्धियाँ आठ प्रकार की हैं।
english: The bone-joints (asthisaṃdhi) are of eight kinds.
notes: Closing 'iti' goes here, not in the translation. Copula understood and supplied. The printed avagraha after -o is regular (saṃdhayaḥ + aṣṭa-).

hindi: स्नायु, पेशी और सिरा पर आश्रितों के साथ तो दो हजार; और शस्त्र के प्रयोग में उनके विषय में कुछ और कहने को नहीं है, इसलिए अलग से नहीं कहा जाता।
english: But together with (ones) resting on ligaments (snāyu), muscles (peśī) and veins (sirā): two thousand. Since nothing more is to be said about them in the application of the surgical instrument (śastrapraṇidhāna), (it) is not stated separately.
notes: OPEN parse (see glossary). The counted noun of 'two thousand' is unstated; the plainest reading is the bone-joints of 154 taken together with those resting on snāyu, peśī and sirā, but the text does not say so. Unstated subject of ucyate shown as '(it)'. 'iti' is read as giving the reason. snāyu = ligament or tendon, peśī = muscle (standard); sirā = vein or blood vessel (probable). śastra = surgical instrument.
lines_deva: स्नायुपेशीसिराश्रितैस्तु सह सहस्रद्वयं न पुनः शस्त्रप्रणिधाने तेषु वाच्यमस्तीति पृथङ्नोच्यते
lines_iast: snāyupeśīsirāśritaistu saha sahasradvayaṃ na punaḥ śastrapraṇidhāne teṣu vācyamastīti pṛthaṅnocyate

hindi: नौ सौ स्नायु यानी बन्धन-तन्तु।
english: Nine hundred ligaments (snāyu).
notes: nava śatāni = nine hundreds = 900.

hindi: उनमें से छह सौ शाखाओं में।
english: Of them, six hundred in the limbs (śākhā).
notes: GROUPING: lines 157-159 (card 145/147) appear to continue 156 as one statement. Limb check: per limb 30 (toes) + 30 (160-162: sole, kūrca, ankle) + 30 + 10 + 40 + 10 = 150, x 4 = 600.

hindi: दो सौ तीस अन्तराधि यानी धड़ में।
english: Two hundred and thirty in the trunk (antarādhi).
notes: triṃśat + śata-dvayam = thirty and two hundred = 230. Check: 600 + 230 + 70 = 900, matching 156.

hindi: ऊपर सत्तर।
english: Seventy above.
notes: As in 132, ūrdhvam is 'above' (probably the neck and head).

hindi: वहाँ प्रत्येक सक्थि यानी सम्भवतः शाखा में, पैर की प्रत्येक उँगली में छह-छह।
english: There, in each single sakthi (probably meaning limb), in each toe (pādāṅguli), six each.

text_flags.why: possible: see line 133 (card 123); the neuter locative would be sakthni, the printed form repeats there

notes: GROUPING: 160-161 appear to belong together. Counted noun unstated (snāyu, from 156). For sakthi see line 133 (card 123); the same printed locative form is flagged there.

hindi: वे तीस हैं।
english: Those are thirty.
notes: Copula understood and supplied. Check: six in each of five toes = 30.

words.gloss: foot; sole; kūrca (a part of the foot); ankle

hindi: तलवे, कूर्च और टखने में दस-दस।
english: Ten each in the sole (pādatala), kūrca and ankle (gulpha).
notes: kūrca is a named part of the foot; left untranslated. The pāda-tala is read as 'sole of the foot'. Print 'kūrcca' has a doubled c, normalised to kūrca (orthographic, recorded once). daśa daśa = ten each.

hindi: तीस जङ्घा यानी घुटने से टखने तक की टाँग में।
english: Thirty in the shank (jaṅghā).
notes: jaṅghā = the lower leg, shank (standard).

hindi: दस जानु यानी घुटने में।
english: Ten in the knee (jānu).

hindi: चालीस ऊरु यानी जाँघ में।
english: Forty in the thigh (ūru).

hindi: दस वंक्षण यानी जाँघ के मूल में।
english: Ten in the groin (vaṅkṣaṇa).

hindi: चालीस कटि यानी कमर में।
english: Forty in the hip (kaṭi).
notes: kaṭi = hip or waist.

words.gloss: scrotum or testes; penis; bladder; intestines

hindi: बीस मुष्क यानी अण्डकोष, मेढ्र यानी लिंग, बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय और अन्त्र यानी आँतों में।
english: Twenty in the muṣka (scrotum or testes), meḍhra (penis), basti (bladder) and antra (intestines).

english: For the body, well bound in the joints by the bonds of sinew (snāva), acts properly, like a boat.
